chapter_title: Concerning the Fasting of the Saints
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by late institutional/pastoral material (fasting practice, saints, weekly observance, alms), with a small embedded cosmological-mechanistic substrate about (a) the soul/light entering via food and (b) the purity-state of the Children of Light. The strong editorial-fatigue signal fits the drift into explicit communal regulation in the final paragraphs.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue/frame attribution (“Once more the enlightener speaks…”) typical of the Kephalaia’s hagiographic/editorial container.
Programmatic statement about fasting ‘the saints’ and its ‘profit’ for four works: an institutional-ethical rubric rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.
Ascetic exhortation logic (“punish his body by fasting”) and moral-anthropological aim (“subdues… ruling-power”) presented as a disciplinary benefit; not a cosmos→cosmos mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: This soul that comes into him in the administration of his food, day by day; it shall be made holy, cleansed, purified, and washed from the adulteration of the Darkness that is mixed in with it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the pastoral/list header (“The second:”) which functions as an editorial structuring device for a four-point ascetic instruction.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying core mechanism: a technical soteriological cosmology of ‘soul’ entering through food and being purified from Darkness-mixture (impersonal process language). The surrounding ‘four works’ scheme is pastoral organization.

paragraphs.core_text: the mystery of [the children] of Light in whom there is neither corruption nor [...] the food, nor wound it. Rather, they are holy, [there is nothing] in them that defiles, as they live in peace.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ascetic exhortation header and moralizing lead-in (“The third: That person shall make every deed a holy one;”) as later pastoral application scaffolding.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core-like descriptive register about the ‘Children of Light’ as a pure order whose being is unaffected by corruption/defilement—cosmic anthropology stated as what they ARE, not what an audience should DO. Embedded within a later fasting-benefits list.

Despite cosmological terms (“the Cross”, “living soul”), the surviving lines are framed as ascetic restraint of hands/actions (ethical practice). The lacunae prevent securely isolating a self-contained older cosmological proposition.
Institutional persistence language (“should they persist… daily… cause the body… members to fast”)—explicit practical discipline; no impersonal cosmological mapping.
Clear community regulation and accommodation (“have not strength… fast on the lord’s day… alms”), consistent with the chapter’s late pastoral drift and institutionalization.
